correctness.rationale: The return of (F_n,F_(n+1)) to (0,1) is equivalent to M^n=I, so scalar periods equal matrix orders. Direct prime-level iteration gives 16 and 10; the two displayed powers are I+pB with unit upper off-diagonal in B. The binomial p-power lift gives v_p(F_(Pt))=1+v_p(t) for nonzero t, which proves the exact prime-power orders; gcd=2 and lcm=80·7^(a−1)·11^(b−1). For a period increment h=Pt with t nonzero, L_h+2 is a unit, so (L_h−2)(L_h+2)=5F_h² gives v_p(L_h−2)=2v_p(F_h). In the Fibonacci addition law, if L_r is a unit the term F_hL_n uniquely has the smallest valuation: the normalized Fibonacci branch is an isometry at each finite precision, giving one preimage per target in its residue disk. The excluded indices are 4 and 12 modulo 16 and 5 modulo 10. In those branches F_r is a unit, so the Lucas addition law instead makes the normalized Lucas map isometric and onto the divisible Lucas classes. The identity L_n²=5F_n²+4(-1)^n, with 10F_r a unit, then identifies the exceptional frequency with R_(p,k). For D=0 the root is divisible by p^ceil(k/2), giving p^floor(k/2) choices (including k=1); nonzero represented D has no root unless its valuation is even and the unit part is a square, and gives 2p^h roots when v_p(D)=2h≥2. Generalized CRT gives one index for each pair of equally paritied local indices, none otherwise. The seven-adic support sizes (even, odd, intersection) are (3A+2Q_7,4A,2A), A=7^(a−1), and eleven-adic sizes are (5B,2B+Q_11,B), B=11^(b−1), with Q at exponents a−2,b−2. Inclusion–exclusion yields the finite formula; Q_p counts squares and its normalized limit is the sum of the even valuation weights, p/[2(p+1)]. Substitution proves the two-variable density and discrepancy, not just a diagonal limit. A fresh recurrence replay checked complete parity tables and the root counts up to local exponent five and every composite fiber and support for all nine exponent pairs in [1,3]², including the stated support values 35, 1755 and 130525.
